hypothesis: RH is equivalent to the positivity of Weil's Hermitian form W(f,g) = sum_rho m_rho f_hat(gamma_rho) conj(g_hat(conj(gamma_rho))) on compactly supported test functions (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000). The finite-dimensional route compresses W to d ~ N(T) modulated copies of a window psi, obtaining a real symmetric matrix G_tilde whose trace and Hilbert-Schmidt norm are evaluated on the prime side, and reads off a proportion of simple on-line zeros via a rank-trace inequality. This is the mechanism of Alpoge-Furman (arXiv:2608.13637), which reaches 2/3 and records that its certificate is sharp within its class and that improving it needs pair-correlation information beyond Fourier support 1.
falsification_criterion: THIS IS THE ONE FRAMING HERE WHOSE NUMERICAL TEST CAN REFUTE RH, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS. If RH holds then W is positive semidefinite, so EVERY finite compression of W is positive semidefinite -- a principal submatrix of a PSD matrix is PSD. Contrapositive: a single negative eigenvalue of a correctly constructed finite compression REFUTES RH. That is a genuine, finite, checkable refutation, and it is sensitive to one off-line pair, which is exactly the sensitivity every statistical argument lacks. The converse is NOT available: a positive compression proves nothing, because a compression is positive whenever its subspace happens to avoid the negative directions, and a finite test family cannot exhaust the space. So the honest reading of a clean numerical result here is 'no refutation found at this truncation', never 'evidence for RH'. Falsified also by an error in the construction: a compression built from the wrong window or the wrong test family tests a different form, and its eigenvalues say nothing about W.
notes: WHAT IMPLEMENTING THE REFUTATION TEST REQUIRES, stated so it is not mistaken for done. The compression needs (1) the explicit formula in the form that expresses W(f,g) as a sum over primes plus archimedean terms, (2) a window psi -- the indicator psi_0 or the Montgomery-Taylor window, with R(psi_0) = 4/3 and R(psi_MT) = c_MT^-1 = 1/2 + (1/sqrt2)cot(1/sqrt2), (3) the d modulated copies equispaced through [T,2T], and (4) the prime-side evaluation of the trace and Hilbert-Schmidt norm. None of that is implemented in this repository. What IS implemented, in python/riemann_framework/proportion_certificates.py, is the linear-algebra half: the rank-trace inequality of item (L) and the constant chain, both checked. The analytic half is out of reach here. Note also that the proportion route cannot reach RH however far it is pushed -- Alpoge-Furman section 1.4 records that the inputs are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros and hold for Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein zeta functions, for which the analogue of RH is FALSE. The compression's NEGATIVE eigenvalues are a different matter, and are the reason this record exists: they are what an off-line pair looks like, via Sylvester's law of inertia, and Bombieri's observation that the negative index counts off-line pairs is the basis. Because numpy.linalg.eigvalsh is not a certified eigenvalue solver, any negative eigenvalue found numerically would need interval arithmetic or a rational reconstruction before it could be called a refutation.
